claims.text: In situ high-temperature X-ray diffraction can monitor time- and temperature-dependent phase formation and transformation during high-temperature oxidation.
Thermogravimetric analysis can continuously monitor oxidation kinetics through mass changes.
Integrated HTXRD and TGA enable simultaneous, continuous monitoring of phase stability and oxidation kinetics.
The starting material has a homogeneous phase structure in its as-prepared, unoxidized state.
HTXRD and mass-change data can be collected concurrently during controlled high-temperature oxidation.
Temperatures of 800–1200°C in an oxygen-rich atmosphere can replicate relevant service conditions.
High-temperature oxidation produces oxide phases in high-temperature materials.
Oxidation can be accompanied by phase transformations detectable as changes in diffraction patterns.
Oxide formation alters the material's crystal structure.
HTXRD captures oxidation-associated phase transitions in real time.
TGA records mass gain or loss associated with oxidation.
Integrating HTXRD and TGA permits correlation of phase evolution with oxidation kinetics.
Integrated HTXRD-TGA will reveal a time-resolved correlation between oxidation-induced phase changes and corresponding mass gain.
Integrated HTXRD-TGA offers more complete insight than separate ex situ approaches.
Previous studies relied on ex situ measurements or separate experiments for oxidation kinetics and phase stability.
Separate ex situ measurements do not capture the full time-dependent interplay between oxidation kinetics and phase stability.
The method may have reduced sensitivity when phase transitions or mass changes are very small.
The resolution of integrated measurements depends on calibration and synchronization of the HTXRD and TGA systems.
Sensitivity and resolution limits may vary among material systems and experimental configurations.
Failure to observe a consistent temporal correlation between XRD-detected phase transformations and TGA mass-change events would falsify the proposed simultaneous-monitoring capability.
